lines.en: The final trial of a king.
An ordeal that pushed you to your limits, one you had to overcome with nothing but your own body.
The ground at Gwanghwamun was riddled with craters.
Thwack! Wham!
With the ‘Absolute Throne’ between them at the center, the kings were locked in a tangled fight.
The King of Beauty, Min Jiwon.
The Maitreya King, Cha Sangkyung.
The Supreme King, Yoo Joonghyuk.
And that middle-aged man standing off in a corner······.
I see. The ‘Neutral King’?
The ‘Neutral King’ met my eyes and raised both hands.
[The ‘Neutral King’, Jeon Ildo, has forfeited.]
As expected, true to his name, the Neutral King had no desire for the throne.
Only the remaining three wanted it.
With Yoo Joonghyuk among those three, this fight should normally have ended in less than 1 minute. Normally, that is.
“Die, you fiend!”
The Maitreya King Cha Sangkyung’s ceremonial staff sliced through the air, and Yoo Joonghyuk’s kick struck Cha Sangkyung in the stomach.
“Guh!”
But Cha Sangkyung took less damage than I’d expected.

That was because everyone’s stats had been changed to an average of 10. With skills sealed as well, the outcome would ultimately depend on muscle memory. Even Yoo Joonghyuk couldn’t subdue the other kings right away.
Min Jiwon, who had been hanging back behind them and watching for an opening, spotted me.
I gave her a slight nod.
“We meet again.”
“······So we do. I didn’t want to fight you.”
If she’d made it this far, Min Jiwon must also have fulfilled all the qualifications of a king. An impressive feat. Honestly, I hadn’t thought she would survive to the end.
“If you don’t forfeit, I’ll attack.”
“Try it. I won’t be an easy opponent.”
A fight with no skills, no stigmas, and average stats of 10. It was a pitiful sight for a battle between kings who had been flying around and demolishing the city just moments ago.
There was a thud, followed by Cha Sangkyung’s scream.
“Gah! W-why...?”
Struck by Yoo Joonghyuk’s fist, Cha Sangkyung was rolling across the ground in pain. The fight had clearly been evenly matched just a moment ago, but its course was gradually changing.
Despite being unable to use skills or stigmas, Yoo Joonghyuk’s attacks were growing faster and faster, harder and harder. It wasn’t simply because he had an exceptional sense for combat.
Min Jiwon seemed surprised, too.
If I remembered correctly, Yoo Joonghyuk discovered the loophole in the ‘final phase’ during this round.
By now, messages like these were probably appearing in Yoo Joonghyuk’s head.
[You have invested 300 coins in Constitution.]
[You have invested 300 coins in Agility.]
[You have invested 300 coins in Strength.]
Funnily enough, this battlefield had ‘restricted everything’ but left one thing unrestricted: the coins each person possessed.
[The constellation ‘Supreme Maegum’ questions the fairness of the scenario.]
The intermediate dokkaebi laughed.

[Haha, what is there to question? Using the coins you possess is your rightful privilege. At least ‘coins’ are something the incarnations worked hard to earn themselves. After working so hard to save them up, they deserve a chance to spend them.]
Yoo Joonghyuk was raising his stats with the coins he had.
[Ah, of course, any stats raised with coins here will be reset after the scenario ends. So be sure to spend carefully! It’s practically the same as throwing your coins away! Hahaha!]

Min Jiwon and Cha Sangkyung’s faces darkened sharply at the intermediate dokkaebi’s words. They probably had hardly any coins left. It was only natural. On a battlefield where kings were trading blows, they wouldn’t have had the luxury of saving coins.
But Yoo Joonghyuk was different.
Having grown stronger by clearing all sorts of hidden scenarios from the outset, Yoo Joonghyuk always kept a reasonable reserve of coins.
In the original third round, Yoo Joonghyuk had about 30,000 coins at this point. He would have earned more coins now than he originally did······ so perhaps he had around 40,000?
With a tremendous thud, Cha Sangkyung’s battered body went flying like a rag.
[The ‘Maitreya King’, Cha Sangkyung, has been rendered unable to fight.]
Yoo Joonghyuk looked at Min Jiwon nearby. She flinched and hurriedly raised both hands.
“······I forfeit.”
[The ‘King of Beauty’, Min Jiwon, forfeits.]
At last, Yoo Joonghyuk looked at me.
His eyes, which had been full of rage, had grown calm.
I could understand why.
Once he claimed the ‘Absolute Throne’, he could control all the kings however he pleased. He must have thought getting his younger sister back from me would be no problem.
But would it really work out that way?
“Yoo Joonghyuk.”
We drew our swords against each other.
Unable to use any skills, I had to rely solely on my muscle memory and the meager overall stats I possessed.
Whoosh!
For the first time, I could see Yoo Joonghyuk’s blade.
It had to be a feint.
He was testing how high my stats were and how many coins I had left.
Cautious as ever.
He was probably planning to win by investing as few coins as possible.
But this time, that arrogance would be your downfall.
Because no ‘king’ in ‘Seoul’ right now would have more coins than I did.
[Coins Held : 80850 C]
After all, who would even think to hold out until they’d saved 80,000 coins?
I grinned at Yoo Joonghyuk as he charged toward me.
“I’ll go easy on you, so don’t die.”
Time to sell it all and cash in my profits.
As though venting all my frustration at being unable to spend coins until now, I invested a huge sum in ‘Strength’.
[You have invested 4000 coins in ‘Strength’.]
[Strength Lv.10 -> Strength Lv.20]
[You have invested 5000 coins in ‘Strength’.]
[Strength Lv.20 -> Strength Lv.30]
[You have invested 6000 coins in ‘Strength’.]
[Strength Lv.30 -> Strength Lv.40]
[You have invested 11000 coins in ‘Strength’.]
[Strength Lv.80 -> Strength Lv.90]
[You have invested 12000 coins in ‘Strength’.]
[Strength Lv.90 -> Strength Lv.100]
[You have spent a total of 72000 coins.]
[Your ‘Strength’ surpasses the limits of human potential.]
[An astounding achievement!　You are the first to reach a three-digit Strength level.]
[You receive 30000 coins as a reward.]
I regulated the power in my fist. A blow with 100 Strength was tremendous. It would be a problem if I accidentally killed Yoo Joonghyuk.
I could feel the space around my fist bending ever so slightly.
According to ‘Ways of Survival’, the moment any overall stat reached three digits, it gained destructive power on an entirely different level.
What did it feel like, you ask?
Killer, of course.
Like clutching a fistful of checks worth hundreds of millions.
I saw Yoo Joonghyuk’s eyes widen as he hurriedly spent his coins.
But it was already too late.
A sonic boom erupted with a sound like a bursting bag of money.
And Yoo Joonghyuk shot into the sky like a baseball struck squarely by a bat.

Unfortunately, home runs were impossible in this stadium. Yoo Joonghyuk hit one barrier, then another on the opposite side. Only after bouncing back and forth like that five or six times did he finally slam into the ground.
······He might actually die from that.
Somewhat flustered, I ran toward Yoo Joonghyuk.
Damn it, why had I done that? I should have held back a little more.
I carefully pulled Yoo Joonghyuk out of the hole he’d sunk into. But then.
Ah, this was why protagonists were.
Yoo Joonghyuk was glaring at me with his eyes wide open.
Wait, he’d taken a fucking blow with 100 Strength and was still lucid?
“······Yoo Joonghyuk?”
“Joonghyuk?”
His eyes didn’t move.
Had this bastard actually passed out with his eyes open?
Had I hit him too hard?
No, when would I ever get another chance to hit Yoo Joonghyuk like this?
“See, you bastard? You should’ve treated me better. Why is threatening to kill me always the first thing you do whenever we meet?”
I gave that face I’d always found so irritating a few brisk slaps. It somehow seemed like his eyeballs moved every time I slapped his cheek, which bothered me······.
Anyway, he was still breathing.
Even if every bone in his body was broken and he was bleeding from all seven openings in his head······.
Since he couldn’t use the ‘Recovery’ skill here, his life could well be in danger.
I had to move things along quickly.
[The ‘Supreme King’, Yoo Joonghyuk, has been rendered unable to fight.]
[Congratulations! You have passed all the trials of the ‘Absolute Throne’.]
The barriers were slowly disappearing from the air.
[The temporary stat increases purchased with coins are being withdrawn.]
[All restrictions placed on the kings are being lifted.]
[The constellation ‘Prisoner of the Golden Headband’ has its fur bristling from the excessive cathartic fizz.]
[The constellation ‘Secretive Plotter’ applauds you for stubbornly holding out.]
[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ marvels at your patience.]
[You have received 4500 coins in sponsorship.]
Messages from the Historical-grade constellations followed.
[The constellation ‘Supreme Maegum’ laments bitterly.]
[The constellation ‘One-Eyed Maitreya’ throws away his eyepatch.]
[The constellation ‘Founder of Hannamgun’ resents you.]
As expected, all the kings of the Later Three Kingdoms resented me.
They had missed one of their few opportunities to advance to ‘Narrative-grade’. They would naturally regret it.
[······Oh, we have an unexpected victor.]
For some reason, the intermediate dokkaebi looked displeased.
He probably hadn’t expected me to win, either.
But I had won.
[Well······ fine. A result is a result. Now, an announcement for all incarnations in Seoul. A new master of the ‘Absolute Throne’ has just been born!]
I stopped the intermediate dokkaebi as he was about to display a system message.
“Wait a moment.”
[······What is it?]
The intermediate dokkaebi’s eyebrow twitched.
“You’re getting ahead of yourself. I haven’t even ascended the throne yet. How can you just announce it? Shouldn’t you ask what I want, too?”
[You are about to ascend it, so what difference does it make?]
I strode toward the ‘Absolute Throne’.
At that moment, I could feel every constellation watching Seoul Dome focusing on me.
The ‘Absolute Throne’, which had risen high into the sky, slowly descended toward me.
Displaying a courteous golden glow, as though it had been waiting for me for a very long time.
I asked the intermediate dokkaebi a question.
“What can I do with this?”
[Anything that can be done to a human.]
A short answer, but a frightening one.

[The ‘Absolute Throne’ is an item that lives up to its name. As long as you sit on that throne, you can wield unlimited authority. No subject on the land you rule will be able to defy you, and everyone will bow before you!]
At the dokkaebi’s explanation, several people looked at me enviously.
Of course they would be envious.
They’d all come this far coveting that seat alone.
[The constellation ‘Supreme Maegum’ smacks their lips.]
Even those constellations······.
It really was both sad and strange.
That they could envy it like that, even knowing this item’s true nature.
I really hated the lot of them, these constellations.
“Is that all?”
[······Pardon?]
“Its abilities are all too good to be true. Enjoying ‘absolute authority’ over the ‘land’ I rule.”
[Isn’t it only natural to be rewarded for your hardships? You reached this throne after escaping death time and again······.]
“Aha, so this throne can even do all that without any ‘probability restrictions’?”
“You’re really good at lying. Is it because you’re a dokkaebi? Does the Bureau have nothing to say about you running a scam like that?”

For a moment, the intermediate dokkaebi failed to control his expression. Then his face hardened. Across the expanse of air, Bihyung was watching me with a look of utter despair. He probably thought I’d finally lost my mind.
[Let’s stop this tiresome argument. It is time to end the scenario. Now, sit on the throne. One more word of nonsense, and I may destroy the ‘Absolute Throne’.]
“······Ah, about that. Do whatever you want.”
[Pardon?]
I looked at the dokkaebi, then turned to the people gaping blankly at me, and slowly spoke.
“I will not ascend this ‘Absolute Throne’.”
A terrible silence swept over Gwanghwamun.
I thought I heard thunder in the sky, and soon rain began to fall.
The light rising from the Absolute Throne reached the sky.
Thick, dark clouds swirling around that light.
An omen of the fifth scenario, the Great Hall (Great hall).
Standing in the steady drizzle, the intermediate dokkaebi spoke.
[······What did you just say?]
“I said I’m not taking the throne.”

[I don’t understand why you are being so obstinate. Don’t you think you would be better off earning even 1 more coin in the time you are wasting? You must have spent an enormous number of coins earlier. Just accept your reward. That
‘Absolute Throne’—without its power, Seoul Dome will never survive the ‘fifth scenario’.]
Perhaps frightened by the dokkaebi’s words, the people gathered around Gwanghwamun shouted at me.
“What? What the hell is he thinking?”
“Quit yammering and just sit down!”
“Damn it, if only I’d gotten that seat instead······!”
Apparently thinking things were going his way, the dokkaebi continued.

[That throne can give you more than you could wish for. Simply sitting on it will build your ‘Story’, and the constellation sponsors contracted to you will rise in Status. You appear not to understand what that means.]
In fact, the constellations had been clamoring in my ears for some time.
[The constellation ‘Adventurer Who Stands Up an Egg’ wishes to become your constellation sponsor.]
[The constellation ‘Seo Ae Il Pil’ wishes to become your constellation sponsor.]
[You have received 500 coins in sponsorship.]
The intermediate dokkaebi continued in a cold voice.
[Let me warn you in advance: I am different from the low-grade dokkaebis. Do not think your clumsy little tricks will work on me.]
I looked down at the ‘Absolute Throne’.
As the dokkaebi had said, clearing the ‘fifth scenario’ would become difficult if I didn’t obtain the ‘Absolute Throne’ here.
But I also knew what the dokkaebi hadn’t said.
If I used this ‘Absolute Throne’ even once, I would never be able to reach the end of the scenarios.
Even the Yoo Joonghyuk of the original novel had only barely realized this in his fourteenth round.
Because that was what this ‘Absolute Throne’ had been from its very creation.
“Why the hell won’t you be king!”
An agitated man emerged from the crowd. Breathing heavily, he pointed an accusing finger at me as though I’d insulted his very life.
I answered him with a question.
“That’s what I’d like to ask you. What makes you trust me enough to make me ‘king’?”
“What?”
“What will you do if I kill you after becoming king?”
The man’s parted lips suddenly froze.
I looked at the other people around us and continued.
“The same goes for all of you. Have you already forgotten? We didn’t originally live in a kingdom. So why are you already acting like a kingdom’s subjects?”
Why didn’t I want to be king?
It was simple.
“I don’t want to be a king who represents ugly human beings like you.”
I looked at the sky and continued.
“And I don’t want filthy constellations like you as my sponsors, either.”
Then I looked at the throne.
“So I will not sit on the ‘Absolute Throne’. But.”
Almost at the same time, I drew my sword.
“I won’t allow anyone else to sit on it, either.”
For someone to take that seat meant someone else couldn’t.
A cold flame flared in the intermediate dokkaebi’s eyes.
[You would do well to stop there. I am not particularly patient······.]
I stared straight at the dokkaebi and kept speaking.
“How much longer will you let yourselves be dragged helplessly through the dokkaebis’ ‘scenarios’? Don’t you have the slightest idea what it means for someone to sit on the ‘Absolute Throne’?”
I knew how steep a price people accustomed to ‘submission’ had to pay to free themselves from that ‘submission’.
“Constellations of the Korean Peninsula. The same goes for you. I know very well that not all constellations are equal. Some constellations have low Status, and others have high Status.”
There was an invisible hierarchy among constellations, too.
Just as constellations watched incarnations, some constellations watched other constellations.
Specifically, constellations of lower Status.
“But isn’t that enough by now? How much longer will you keep making this land a battleground for unfortunate historical figures?”
[The constellation ‘One-Eyed Maitreya’ lets out a low murmur.]

“You struggle to build a history and become Historical-grade constellations, then build Stories and become Narrative-grade constellations······ and what will you do next? Once you’ve become brighter stars in a higher sky? How far must you go in exploiting the descendants of this land for your own selfish interests before you’re satisfied?”
[The constellation ‘Supreme Maegum’ falls silent.]
That was when the intermediate dokkaebi, who had been silent, moved.
[I can no longer stand by and watch.]
At those words, a system message arrived.
[A new ‘sub-scenario’ has arrived.]
<Sub-Scenario ― Forced Succession Ceremony>
Category : Sub
Difficulty : B
Clear Conditions : Subdue the incarnation ‘Kim Dokja’, who refuses to sit on the throne, and seat him upon it.
Time Limit : 30 minutes
Reward : 6000 coins
Upon Failure : ―
Right. I’d known he would resort to this in the end.
The people who had briefly wavered at my words were approaching me.
In the end, the dokkaebi was right. Those people, and me, too. However eloquently we spoke, we were nothing but vermin who sold our consciences for a handful of coins.
Of course, not everyone was like that.
“Try getting past me, if you can.”
A woman stood in front of me, blocking their way.
At her snarling voice, the people faltered.
It was Jung Heewon.
“Whatever happens to the world, there are things we must never forget.”
Yoo Sangah had approached as well. Hammer in hand, Lee Gilyoung guarded my back as though he’d been waiting for this. Jung Minseob and Lee Sungkook, who had been standing by, came over, too.
“······Sometimes you seem more like the protagonist than Yoo Joonghyuk, Representative-nim.”
“Even Yoo Joonghyuk wouldn’t do something this crazy······.”
Some unexpected people joined them.
“I’m only helping you this once.”
“Our royal mind-reading tells Us your words were persuasive.”
The King of Beauty, Min Jiwon, and even the Maitreya King, Cha Sangkyung.
I didn’t know what in my words had moved their hearts.
But something had certainly changed.
Even if it amounted to less than a handful of possibility in this world.
[Look at the vermin playing together······ What are you doing? Drag them away at once!]
The people charged toward the throne.
Pushing back the ranks of people right beside me, Jung Heewon asked,
“Dokja-ssi, you have something in mind, don’t you?”
“Yes.”
“What should we do?”
“Buy me some time. Until I destroy this ‘throne’.”
The path to a new scenario lay inside this ‘throne’.
I took a sword from inside my clothes.
Someone in the crowd shouted.
“It’s the Four Tiger Evil Cutting Sword!”
The Four Tiger Evil Cutting Sword was an S+ grade item.

But if certain conditions were met, it could briefly be turned into a ‘Star Relic’. Because the Four Tiger Evil Cutting Sword was an item Historical-grade constellations had poured their souls into forging.
[Activating the special option of ‘Ganpyeongui’: ‘Echo of the Stars’.]
[Through ‘Echo of the Stars,’ you can request help from Historical-grade constellations.]
“I will call upon a constellation.”
[Historical-grade constellations hear your voice amid the flow of stars.]
As though reciting an incantation, I called out the constellations’ modifiers.
“I seek the ‘First Star Lord of the Big Dipper’.”
Star Lord Tamnang (貪狼).
“I seek the ‘Second Star Lord of the Big Dipper’.”
Star Lord Geomun (巨文).
“I seek the ‘Third Star Lord of the Big Dipper’.”
Star Lord Nokjon (祿存).
“I seek the ‘Fourth Star Lord of the Big Dipper’.”
Star Lord Mungok (文曲).
“I seek the ‘Fifth Star Lord of the Big Dipper’.”
Star Lord Yeomjeong (廉貞).
“I seek the ‘Sixth Star Lord of the Big Dipper’.”
Star Lord Mugok (武曲).
[The stars begin their passage.]
[Six constellations look at you.]

As all the star patterns vanished from the celestial plate, my head felt as cramped as a packed subway car. I staggered with dizziness, and blood flowed from my nose and ears at the same time. Even thinking was a struggle. Contact with six constellations at once had overloaded my brain. The Constellations of the Big Dipper spoke.
[What could you be thinking?]
[If you call upon all of us like this.]
[Your mind will be utterly destroyed.]
[Why have you called us?]
[Why do you refuse to take the easy path······.]
[And choose a path of thorns instead?]
But I didn’t stop. To use the Four Tiger Evil Cutting Sword, I still had to call one more constellation. Yet there were no star patterns left on the celestial plate.
[You have exhausted all uses of ‘Ganpyeongui’.]
I took out the jar I’d obtained from the Tyrant King earlier, the [Dragon Jar].
The reward from the seven-person dungeon, [Chamber of the Dragon Jar].
Then I placed two items inside the jar.
“With the S grade item [Three-Ring Loop] as a sacrifice, restore the expended uses of the S grade item [Ganpyeongui].”
[The ‘Dragon Jar’ exerts its wondrous power of restoration.]
[The S grade item ‘Three-Ring Loop’ has disappeared as a sacrifice.]
[The expended uses of the S grade item ‘Ganpyeongui’ have been restored.]
I used [Ganpyeongui] again.
And called the one remaining constellation.
“I seek the ‘Seventh Star Lord of the Big Dipper’.”
Star Lord Pagun (破軍).
Seven stars embroidered upon the air.
At last, all seven constellations (七座) that formed the Big Dipper had gathered.
The seven stars spoke to me at once.
[What do you desire from us?]
“Constellations of the Big Dipper, I wish to sever the bond of a star pattern. Please lend me your sword.”
[······Do you know what that means?]
“I do.”
Precisely because I knew so well, I had risked doing this.
The [Absolute Throne], the final reward of the fourth scenario.
That throne was an item that borrowed the power of one of the ‘Outer Gods’.
Obtaining the throne would make things easier for the moment. I could place restrictions on Yoo Joonghyuk, and the enemies threatening me from within would disappear.
But Seoul would inevitably be destroyed.
Utter ruin, without any salvation or miracle.
That was the price of recklessly borrowing ‘absolute’ power.
To reach the ending I had in mind, no one could be allowed to possess that throne.
[Even the constellations of this sky are wary of the throne’s creator.]
[Yet you, a mere human, would challenge that object’s master?]
“I can do it if you help me. And I’m not fighting its master. I’m merely cutting the star pattern that connects the master to the object.”
[That is a burden of probability you cannot bear.]
[You will certainly die.]
“That’s for me to decide. Let’s begin.”
The seven constellations fell silent. How much time passed? The Big Dipper shone brightly in the sky, and the star pattern engraved on the sword blazed with light.
[We respect your will.]
[Even if you die here.]
[We will remember you.]
Dazzling rays of light wound around the Four Tiger Evil Cutting Sword, and its white blade began to burn with brilliant flames.
[The S+ grade item ‘Four Tiger Evil Cutting Sword’ evolves into the Star Relic ‘Four Tiger Evil Cutting Sword’.]
The Star Relic Four Tiger Evil Cutting Sword was a ceremonial sword originally made for ‘ritual offerings’.
A sword that severed evil energies and warded off calamity.
I swung the sword straight at the ‘Absolute Throne’.
Sparks flew with a clang.
The Four Tiger Evil Cutting Sword was one of the few items capable of severing the bond (緣) linking a constellation to a ‘Star Relic’.
Cra-a-ack.
I heard something tearing in the unseen expanse of air.

As though it had begun to notice something, the ‘Absolute Throne’ was wreathed in an ominous black glow. After a few more blows against it, the Four Tiger Evil Cutting Sword’s edge began to chip. From this point on, I had no choice but to trust the Constellations of the Big Dipper. Yoo Sangah shouted.
“Dokja-ssi! Hurry!”
I swung the sword like a madman.
Ignoring the damage to the blade, I kept striking the throne.
Bursting sparks and a shattering blade.
And at last.
[The blessing linked to the Star Relic ‘Absolute Throne’ disappears.]
[An ‘Unknown God’ has noticed the upheaval in this world.]
The ‘Absolute Throne’ lost its light, becoming an ordinary chair.
I heard the flabbergasted intermediate dokkaebi scream in rage.
[That vermin who doesn’t know his place·······!]
[The sub-scenario has been forcibly terminated.]
The people stopped moving, too. With the scenario over, they no longer had any reason to continue. The Constellations of the Big Dipper spoke to me.
[Incarnation, prepare for the coming flood of probability.]
The instant I heard their voices, my stomach churned and blood poured from my mouth.

It felt as though someone were stretching my existence, then pulling it back. An immense force that seemed capable of tearing my body apart circled innocently around me. I struggled to steady my mind. I would be all right.
‘Probability’ ultimately meant ‘plausibility’. Until now, I’d done everything I could to make all these events seem plausible. So I could withstand this.
Repeating that to myself, I barely clung to my fading consciousness.
That was when a single star quietly twinkled in the distant night sky.
[The constellation ‘Maritime War God’ looks at you.]
A single gaze, quiet and lonely, yet very gentle.
[The constellation ‘Bald General of Justice’ looks at you.]
And two.
[The constellation ‘The Last Hero of Hwangsanbeol’ looks at you.]
Three.
[The constellation ‘Supreme Maegum’ looks at you.]
Amid the flood of messages from the constellations, the intermediate dokkaebi shouted.
[Why on earth······?]
With each additional star, my pain lessened a little. I realized the constellations were each taking a small share of the ‘probability’ I had to bear. An ‘implausible story’ was, with so many
stars’ assent, becoming a ‘plausible story’. Countless stars were enveloping me in their light. Among them were the Constellations of the Big Dipper, who had lent me their power.
[Is this the story you wished to show us?]
I wanted to answer, but I didn’t have the strength.
[We will be watching you, ‘King of a Kingless World’.]
Seoul’s tumultuous night sky.
I looked back at the stars sending me their light.
[The constellation ‘King Heungmu the Great’ looks at you.]
[The constellation ‘One-Eyed Maitreya’ looks at you.]
Every Historical-grade constellation in Seoul was shining its light toward me.
Even with so many stars.
They were still not enough to illuminate the dark night sky.
I quietly looked up at the Great Hall raging with the dark clouds.
[The fourth scenario is being forcibly terminated.]
[An unscheduled branch has occurred. Calculating the scenario settlement will take time.]
As I wiped the blood running from my nose, the intermediate dokkaebi strode over.
[You have made the worst possible choice after all. You will bitterly regret what you did today for the rest of your life. On my honor, I will make certain of it.]
Even as my vision blurred, I couldn’t help smiling. The dokkaebi’s words meant I had won.
[You have earned an achievement that did not exist.]
[Your new Story is being created.]
[The Story ‘King of a Kingless World’ has been born.]
[You have obtained the potential for a stigma.]
There was no next ‘round’ for me.
In this world, I would reach the end of the story.
I had built my first Story.
With that, I’d achieved my main objective for the fourth scenario.
“What the hell is about to happen?”
“No, why did you destroy the throne!”
People bewildered because they didn’t understand the situation, and people who immediately panicked at what the angry dokkaebi might do.
In their eyes, I was an unforgivable criminal who had made the ‘fifth scenario’ harder. Some even shouted at the dokkaebi.
“Make the ‘Absolute Throne’ again! We’ll take part in the scenario again!”
“This time, let’s determine the true master of the throne!”
[No one can change a scenario that has already ended. So everything that happens to you from this moment on is that human’s fault.]
The intermediate dokkaebi’s reply was icy.
The dokkaebi pointed at me, and the cold wind and rain shook the drenched people’s shoulders.
[A kingless world? Very well. Try living in it. Let’s see how well you survive without anyone to unite you.]
The intermediate dokkaebi snapped his fingers. The people at Gwanghwamun began disappearing like smoke, one after another. People screamed and fled.
“What the hell! What’s happening all of a sudden!”
······This wasn’t a development I’d expected.
When I turned, Jung Heewon, Yoo Sangah, Lee Gilyoung, and the rest of my companions were calling for me.
“Dokja-ssi!”

The next moment, Yoo Sangah vanished. Then Lee Gilyoung, Jung Heewon. Even Jung Minseob and Lee Sungkook.
